data.title: Suspicious customs fee demand for held parcel
data.summary: A letter claiming to be from a parcel centre's customs department demands €38.90 in import charges by 9 November 2026 for a held parcel. It shows several signs of a scam.
data.explanation: This letter says a parcel from outside the EU is held and asks you to transfer €38.90 to a private company account by 9 November 2026. Real customs charges are normally collected by the carrier or German customs (Zoll) through official channels, not by bank transfer to an unknown company with contact only via WhatsApp. Do not pay yet. Check whether you are actually expecting a parcel, and contact the carrier or customs using contact details you find yourself, not those in this letter. If in doubt, ask a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police.

items.title: Pay parcel import charges (suspicious)
items.action: Do not pay until you have verified the demand with the carrier or customs using contact details you found yourself.
items.consequence: The letter says the parcel would be returned to the sender or destroyed at your cost.

warnings: Payment is requested to a private company (Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.), not to customs or a known carrier.
Queries are accepted only via WhatsApp, and the e-mail domain looks generic, which is typical of scams.
The letter sets a very short deadline and threatens to destroy the parcel, which is a pressure tactic.
The letter gives no tax notice, customs office or legal remedy instructions.
